Two REPL bugs, and the second one needed a real terminal to see.

### A macro defined at the REPL was unbound on the next line

```
>>> (define-syntax swap! (syntax-rules () ((_ a b) (let ((t a)) (set! a b) (set! b t)))))
>>> (swap! p q)
Error: unbound variable swap!
```

The REPL evaluates one form at a time, and `Machine.Run` compiled each one.  A
compiled `define-syntax` expands its uses where it is compiled and defines
nothing — right inside a body, wrong for a sequence of top-level forms.  `Run`
now sends a form that teaches the compiler something to the tree-walker, the
distinction `CompileProgram` already made for whole files.

### Pasting a multi-line expression wrote over the lines above it

```
GoScheme 3.1.2 (R7RS)
Type (exit) or press Ctrl->>> (+ 1
 2)
```

The line editor tracks the row the cursor is on so a redraw can go back up to
the prompt row first.  It was computing that row as the newlines *after* the
cursor — which is zero whenever the cursor is at the end of the line, so after a
paste it thought it was still on the prompt row.  The redraw then rewrote the
row it was on instead of the row above, and every following keystroke stacked
another copy of the prompt down the screen.

It now counts the rows *before* the cursor, which is what GNU readline does with
`_rl_last_v_pos`, and erases from the prompt row down before rewriting, so a
line that has become shorter does not leave its old rows behind.

### How it was found

Not by piping input into the interpreter: piped input never reaches the line
editor, which is why the first two attempts at fixing this kept passing their
tests.  It needs a terminal.  The reproduction drives a pty and renders it with
`pyte`, a real terminal emulator, then reads the resulting screen — which shows
the damage directly:

```
'>>> (define (fact n))'
'  (if (= n 0)r press Ctrl-D to leave.'     <- the banner, overwritten
```

Nine shapes are covered: one line, several lines, a six-line definition, two
pastes in a row, a paste ending in a blank line, a paste into the middle of a
typed line, a paste onto a history entry, typing the first line and pasting the
rest, and backspacing a pasted line back down to one row.  The tests are
`TestPasteIsRedrawnWhereTheCursorIs`, `TestBackspaceAfterPasteStaysOnOneRow`
and `TestMacroVisibleToTheNextForm`.
